_comment: Archivist Ilsabet Thornmere, half-elf scribe of the Oasis Wardens (Scripts/talking_vendor_npc.gd; placed in lumora_outskirts3d.tscn). Sells the spell and skill scrolls of the light and neutral classes (Data/vendor_shop.json 'lumora_scribe_light'); she will not copy the dark classes' texts — Xalvyr Tenn at the bazaar does. Precise, formal, quietly proud of the archive; corrects people's spelling. {word} in a line is a clickable keyword (Scripts/npc_conversation.gd). ALL LINES ARE DRAFTS for the user to change.
greeting: Welcome to the Wardens' {archive}. Mind the ink; it is older than you are.
Good day. If you are here to learn, you are in the right place. If you are here to browse, kindly browse quietly.
Ah, a reader. They are rarer than you would think, in a desert.
shop_intro: Every scroll here is copied by hand from the Wardens' own texts. Every word is checked twice.
Choose carefully. A technique learned badly is worse than one never learned at all.
These are the disciplines of the {light}, and of every honest trade besides. Anything darker, you will not find on my shelves.
ambient: Fourteen copies of the same prayer this week, and not one smudge. Aurethiel be thanked.
No, it is spelled with two L's. It has always been spelled with two L's.
The sand gets into everything. The pages, the ink, my patience.
Half of what I copy is sword drills. The other half is people asking me to explain them.
If you see a {Vol'kyne} with inky fingers down by the stalls, you did not buy anything from me.
secret: Some nights I copy the old texts just to hear the pages turn. The archive is very quiet after dark.
My mother's people kept their histories in song. I keep mine in ink. I am not sure which of us chose better.
There is a shelf in the archive the Wardens keep locked. I have the key. I have never used it.

lines: The Oasis Wardens have kept records since before Lumora had walls. I keep the copies, so the originals survive the rest of you.
The Wardens guard the Light of Solara. I guard what they have learned about using it. It is less glamorous, but it lasts longer.
Xalvyr Tenn. The Sandveil Order keeps him, and he copies whatever they are paid for. I would not trust a single line he writes, and I would not stand downwind of his ink either.
